hints: Focus on what sulfur dioxide becomes in moist air, think acid rain and its reducing power.
Remember that $\text{SO}_2$ is a good reducing agent that is itself oxidised to $\text{SO}_3$, so it can reduce another oxidising pollutant like $\text{NO}_2$.
Now link acid rain to lakes and to limestone, what happens to aquatic life in acidic water and to $\text{CaCO}_3$ in acid?
walkthrough:
**Recall the chemistry of sulfur dioxide**

Think of $\text{SO}_2$ as doing two jobs in the air. It is a reducing agent, and with oxygen and water it forms acid rain.

$$2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$

**Check statement 1 - reduction of NO2**

$\text{NO}_2$ to $\text{NO}$ is a reduction, it gains an electron or loses oxygen. $\text{SO}_2$ can supply that by being oxidised itself to $\text{SO}_3$ or sulfate. So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 - aquatic life**

Sulfuric acid rain runs off into rivers and lakes and lowers the pH. Most fish and aquatic organisms cannot survive in strongly acidic water, so populations fall. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 - limestone statues**

Limestone and marble are mainly $\text{CaCO}_3$, a base that reacts readily with acid.

$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This dissolves and pits the stone surface, which we call corrosion. So statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the conclusions**

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, choose the option that includes all three.

options.A: Correct. All three statements follow from $\text{SO}_2$ chemistry. It reduces $\text{NO}_2$ to $\text{NO}$ while being oxidised, and its acid rain product $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ both acidifies lakes to harm aquatic life and attacks $\text{CaCO}_3$ statues.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination includes only 1 and 2 and leaves out 3. Students choose this if they forget that acid rain reacts with carbonates, but limestone corrosion by acid rain is a classic effect.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes only 2 and 3 and leaves out 1. Students choose this if they remember only acid rain effects and miss that $\text{SO}_2$ is also a reducing agent capable of reducing $\text{NO}_2$.
options.D: Incorrect. This is 1 only. Students choose this if they focus only on the redox reaction and forget the much more famous environmental consequences of acid rain on water and stone.
